title: 3 Enoch, or The Hebrew Book of Enoch
author: Hugo Odeberg (ed)
description: 3 Enoch, or The Hebrew Book of Enoch, edited and translated for the first time with introduction, commentary and critical notes by Hugo Odeberg (Cambridge University Press, 1928), with the Hebrew text. Also known as Sefer Hekhalot, the book belongs to Merkavah and Hekhalot mysticism and was probably redacted between the fifth and ninth centuries CE. It presents Rabbi Ishmael's ascent through the heavenly palaces to the divine throne, where he meets Metatron, who reveals that he was once the patriarch Enoch, transformed into a fiery angelic being, enthroned as the 'lesser YHWH' and prince of the divine presence. Metatron describes the angelic hierarchies, the celestial court, the curtain (pargod) on which all history is written, the souls of the righteous and the wicked, and the cosmic secrets. Odeberg's edition is a landmark of Jewish mysticism scholarship and a key link between apocalyptic Enoch literature and Kabbalah.
